from.place: proof step (2): derived direct image preserves set-indexed direct sums

title: Derived direct image preserves direct sums
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a quasi-compact, quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. For every set-indexed family $(E_i)$ of objects of $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category], the canonical map $\bigoplus_i Rf_*E_i\to Rf_*(\bigoplus_i E_i)$ [def-pc-derived-direct-image] is an isomorphism.

proof.text: This is exactly the direct-sum preservation theorem stated by [lem-pc-derived-direct-image-preserves-direct-sums], with the same hypotheses and the same canonical comparison map; hence that node proves the present statement.

lean.statement: theorem derivedDirectImagePreservesDirectSums {X Y : Scheme.{u₁}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f] [HasDerivedCategory.{w₁} (SheafOfModules.{u₁} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))] [HasDerivedCategory.{w₂} (SheafOfModules.{u₁} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))] : ∀ (I : Type u₁) (E : I → schemeDerivedQCohCategory X), PreservesColimit (Discrete.functor (fun i => (E i).obj)) (schemeDerivedDirectImage f)
lean.note: Reuses the landed declaration for lem-pc-derived-direct-image-preserves-direct-sums. PreservesColimit of the discrete quasi-coherent family is equivalent to invertibility of the canonical direct-sum comparison (Mathlib PreservesCoproduct); ambient derived coproducts exist by lem-pc-derived-ambient-direct-sums.
